CFIS — Complete Technical Report
Generated: 2026-08-25T18:29:05+05:00
Prepared by: AI assistant (Copilot CLI runtime in VS Code)
Executive summary:
CFIS is a web application for collecting, storing, and analyzing corporate carbon emissions data. It is composed of a React single-page frontend and a Node.js + Express backend. The backend persists data via Sequelize into a SQLite database file for the current deployment.
Main backend components and their purpose:
• server.js — Application entry point. Initializes Express, global middleware (CORS, helmet, JSON body parser), mounts API routes, and starts the HTTP server.
• config/database.js — Sequelize configuration. Currently configured to use the sqlite dialect with a file-based storage at backend/cfis.sqlite. This centralizes connection options and logging behavior.
• models/ (Sequelize models) — Domain models include User, Company, CompanyMember, Department, EmissionData, BillUpload, and AuditLog. models/index.js wires associations (hasMany / belongsTo). These models represent the persistent data shape and relationships used across the API.
• middleware/auth.js — Authentication and authorization utilities. Implements JWT validate/verify, a ROLE_PERMISSIONS map for centralized capabilities, helper functions (hasPermission, requirePermission), and company-scoped membership checks used across routes.
• routes/ — Organized REST endpoints: auth (login/register), company (CRUD and admin delete), companyMembers (invite, list, remove with self-removal protection), departments, emissions (manual entry, list, delete, and CSV export), baseline and ai analytics, OCR and bill upload handlers. Each route enforces permission/membership checks provided by middleware/auth.js.
• utils/logAudit.js (or equivalent) — Centralized audit logging used to record sensitive actions such as company deletion and data export, storing entries in AuditLog for compliance and traceability.
• uploads/ — Local filesystem area for bill/pdf/uploads. BillUpload model stores metadata and path references. OCR pipelines consume these files and may create EmissionData records.
• ml/ — Trained machine learning artifacts (joblib files) and scripts used by analytics endpoints (baseline, forecasting, anomaly detection). These are invoked by server-side analytics endpoints as part of processing.
Main frontend components and their purpose:
• src/index.js — React entry; mounts App component and wraps the application with AuthContext provider for authentication state.
• src/App.js — Router definitions and route protection. Uses ProtectedRoute for role-based page access and public routes for onboarding/login.
• src/context/AuthContext.js — Central auth state management: holds current user, JWT token, login/logout helpers and exposes useAuth hook to components.
• src/utils/api.js — Axios wrapper configured with baseURL and automatic Authorization header injection. Central place to handle HTTP errors, token refreshes, and API calls.
• src/pages/* — Page components that implement user flows: Dashboard, CompanyProfile, Companies (admin), Departments, DataCollection (manual emission entry), BillUpload, Baseline/Analytics. UI controls are conditionally rendered based on role and membership data from AuthContext and API responses.
• src/components/Layout.js — Main navigation and layout. Shows/hides navigation items based on user.role and membership roles; connects to ProtectedRoute for access gating.
Technologies used and where they are implemented:
• Node.js + Express — Backend server framework handling HTTP routing, middleware, and request lifecycle (server.js and routes/).
• Sequelize ORM — Data models and DB access implemented in backend/models/*.js and configured in backend/config/database.js. Models map to tables persisted in SQLite file.
• SQLite (sqlite3) — File-based persistence; storage path set in config/database.js. Suitable for development and small deployments; consider Postgres for production scale.
• JSON Web Tokens (jsonwebtoken) — Authentication tokens issued and verified in middleware/auth.js and auth routes; frontend stores and sends tokens via Axios wrapper.
• bcryptjs — Password hashing for user credentials in auth flows.
• multer, pdf-parse, tesseract.js — File uploads and OCR pipeline implemented in upload/ocr routes. multer handles multipart forms, pdf-parse extracts text from PDFs, tesseract.js performs OCR on images when needed.
• xlsx and csv-parser — Excel and CSV processing for imports/exports. Emissions export endpoint builds CSV in backend and returns as attachment (consider streaming for large exports).
• React (Create React App) — Frontend SPA implementation with components and pages in frontend/src. Build using react-scripts produces static assets in frontend/build.
• Axios — HTTP client used by frontend to call API endpoints and attach auth tokens (src/utils/api.js).
• Tailwind / CSS — Styling via utility classes in components. Confirm exact system by checking frontend/package.json (tailwind dependency may or may not be present).
• ML artifacts (joblib) — Pretrained models stored in backend/ml and used by baseline/analytics endpoints to produce forecasts and detect anomalies.
How these technologies integrate (implementation details):
• Request flow: Frontend issues API calls via Axios to backend endpoints (protected with JWT). Backend authenticates via middleware/auth.js and enforces permissions and company membership checks. Routes call Sequelize models to read/write data to SQLite. Sensitive actions call logAudit to record an AuditLog entry.
• Authorization: Central ROLE_PERMISSIONS map provides a single source of truth for capabilities. Company-scoped access additionally queries CompanyMember to allow company_rep members to manage company resources even when not the company owner. Admin role has global overrides for management and destructive operations.
• File handling: Uploaded bills are accepted via multer, stored in uploads/ with metadata in BillUpload. OCR/parsing jobs process these files (pdf-parse or tesseract.js) and create or suggest EmissionData records. The OCR route enforces membership checks before confirming/committing extracted data.
• Analytics: EmissionData is aggregated by baseline/ai endpoints which may load ML artifacts (joblib) from backend/ml. These endpoints are guarded by membership/role checks and return summaries/forecasts to the frontend for visualization.
• Export: Emissions export endpoint is protected with requirePermission('exportCarbonFootprintData') and a company membership check (admin or company_rep/auditor member). It builds a CSV response with selected fields and logs the export action via AuditLog.
Security, auditing and operational notes:
• Credentials & secrets: JWT secret, email credentials, and DB connection should be configured via environment variables and not committed in source control.
• Audit: AuditLog records critical actions. Recommend expanding to capture permission-denied attempts for forensic visibility.
• Backups & scaling: SQLite is appropriate for development and small deployments. For production, migrate to Postgres/MySQL for concurrent write capacity, backups, and scaling. Implement periodic backups if continuing with SQLite.
Recommendations and next steps:
1. Add environment-driven DB config to support Postgres in production, and prepare a migration script to transfer data from SQLite.
2. Convert CSV export to streaming implementation if large datasets are expected, to avoid memory pressure.
3. Extend AuditLog coverage to record permission-denied attempts and other security-relevant events.
4. Harden frontend UX by hiding controls that users are unauthorized to use and show clear messages when actions require higher permissions.
5. Add integration tests for permission flows, company membership behaviors, export, and OCR confirmation flows.
End of report.
